planting.note: Also plantable in spring; container-grown stock establishes either season.

directions: Bacciflava is an old English holly selection grown for berries that ripen clear butter-yellow instead of the species' usual red, held against the same glossy, spiny dark-green foliage through winter. As a female clone it needs a male English holly within range to pollinate its flowers before the yellow fruit will set. Give it well-drained, humus-rich soil and shelter from drying winter wind, which can scorch exposed leaves. Prune lightly in late winter if shaping is wanted, since next year's flower buds form on the current season's growth.

planting.note: Also plantable in spring; container-grown stock establishes either season.

directions: Pyramidalis is a female English holly prized for setting its heavy crop of bright red berries without a separate male pollinator nearby, unusual among hollies and useful where space allows for only one plant. Its naturally dense, conical form and smoother, less heavily spined leaves than typical English holly need little pruning to hold a tidy shape. Grow in well-drained, acidic to neutral soil with shelter from harsh winter sun and wind to prevent leaf scorch. Light shaping after the berry display fades in late winter keeps the pyramid form crisp.

planting.note: Also plantable in spring; container-grown stock establishes either season.

directions: Handsworth New Silver is a Victorian-era English holly selection, raised at the Handsworth nurseries near Sheffield, valued for broad, white-margined leaves carried on distinctive purple-tinged young stems. It is a female clone and needs a male English holly growing nearby to produce its red winter berries against the variegated foliage. Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil with some shelter from scorching winter sun, which can brown the pale leaf margins. Remove any all-green reverted shoots promptly, since they grow more vigorously and can crowd out the variegated growth.

planting.note: Also plantable in spring; container-grown stock establishes either season.

directions: Known as hedgehog holly, Ferox is one of the oldest named English holly selections, documented since the sixteenth century, and is instantly recognizable for bearing short spines scattered across the upper leaf surface in addition to the usual marginal spines. It is a male clone that never produces berries but is grown purely for its curious, densely bristled foliage and slow-growing, compact habit. Site it in well-drained, humus-rich soil in a spot where visitors won't brush against the unusually spiny leaves. It needs almost no pruning beyond removing wayward shoots to keep its naturally neat outline.

planting.note: Also plantable in spring; container-grown stock establishes either season.

directions: Despite its name, Silver Queen is a male English holly, so it never sets berries, but it earns its place for new shoots that emerge purple-pink before maturing into broad, creamy white-margined leaves on purple-flushed stems. Its pollen is useful for setting fruit on nearby female English holly cultivars such as Bacciflava or Handsworth New Silver. Grow in well-drained, acidic to neutral soil with some protection from harsh winter sun to keep the variegated margins from scorching. Remove any shoots that revert to solid green, since they outgrow and can swamp the variegated wood.
